stem: A nurse is using the current CDC Child and Adolescent Immunization Schedule to make a vaccine recommendation. Which approach follows the schedule correctly?

options.A: Use the age table only and ignore catch-up intervals, medical indications, notes, and contraindications
options.B: Determine recommendations by age, then review catch-up intervals, medical indications, notes, and contraindications/precautions
options.C: Restart every vaccine series whenever a child is behind schedule
options.D: Choose vaccines only from the parent’s preferred timing without consulting the schedule

rationale: The current CDC schedule directs healthcare professionals to determine vaccines by age, review catch-up intervals, assess additional recommendations by medical indication, review notes for intervals and special situations, and review contraindications and precautions.
educational_objective: Use all components of the current CDC child/adolescent immunization schedule when making vaccine recommendations.
source_document_title: Child and Adolescent Immunization Schedule by Age (Addendum updated July 2, 2025)
source_version_date: July 2, 2025 schedule; currently operative in 2026 pursuant to the March 16, 2026 preliminary court order
source_locator: Purpose and How to use the schedule, steps 1–5
source_claim_supported: Healthcare providers should use the age table, catch-up table, medical-indication table, notes, and contraindications/precautions when making recommendations.
blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Health Promotion and Maintenance, printed p.9 / PDF p.13
correction_summary: Replaced a vague claim about who develops the schedule with a current, directly verifiable question about how clinicians are instructed to use the schedule; currentness explicitly reflects the 2026 court-order notice.
audit_findings: B reproduces the current CDC five-step use process. A omits required components; C and D contradict use of the schedule. No second answer remains.
audit_reviewer: GPT-5.6 Sol Rule 1 — final semantic audit
